the laboratory that remembers

what enzyme catalysis becomes when machines keep the memory

a vision assembled from what is already being built

adventure · a visionary sketch · 2026

the dream in one sentence

A self-driving enzyme-engineering laboratory whose entire memory is a knowledge graph.

No lab notebook. No human transcription. No result whose provenance cannot be walked.

the machines that produce the data describe it themselves, so the metadata is right by construction rather than by discipline.

the loop, closed

designmodels propose the library
→
build + testthe robot runs the screen
→
learnthe graph absorbs the evidence
  • design — ML-assisted enzyme design, already published practice in the group
  • build + test — LARA: growth, expression, lysis, purification, assay — one robotic line
  • learn — every result lands already semantically described, linked to ChEBI, Rhea, UniProt
  • and the loop turns again — overnight, unattended, documented by construction

reproducibility stops being a virtue and becomes a property of the infrastructure.

one graph, three worlds

the lab

every screen, every mutant, every failure — captured by the machines that ran them

the world

ChEBI, Rhea, UniProt — the curated public memory of biochemistry

joined by shared identifiers, queried as one.

ask: which enzyme converts this substrate, under these conditions, on what evidence? — and the answer cites experiments, not opinions.

the dark matter

most of what a screen produces is failure — and today, failure is thrown away.

every lab re-explores sequence space that another lab already knows is dead.

in the dream, the failures are kept — and the map of what does not work becomes as queryable as the successes.

this is what FAIR data is actually for. not compliance — collective memory.

what becomes findable

find

enzymes on demand — a transaminase for this substrate becomes a query, then a campaign, not a three-year project

see

the complete causal chain behind every number — nothing untraceable, nothing irreproducible

know

the sequence–function landscape of enzyme families as a navigable object — each claim backed by a walkable experiment, each hole in knowledge visible, and plannable as the next automated campaign.

from molecule to process

quantum calculationthe mechanism
→
mutant kineticsthe enzyme
→
reactor yieldthe process

today these are mutually unintelligible subfields — incompatible formats, no shared vocabulary, data locked in group-local spreadsheets.

in the dream they are one graph, and a question can cross the silos.

open by construction

the dream is not a proprietary self-driving lab behind a corporate firewall.
  • the robots are commodity hardware
  • the software is free — GPL and MIT, maintained in the open
  • the standards are open — SiLA2, RDF, SPARQL, JSON-LD
  • the knowledge is shared — FAIR by default

a small academic lab gets the same machine.

the bricks already laid

layer of the dreamalready running
the robotLARA — automated enzyme screening, in production since 2016
the protocolSiLA2 — the open standard for instrument communication
the data formatSciDatS — scientific data as JSON-LD
the semanticsontologies + SPARQL — measured: 18,115 real reactions classified in 80 s
the learningML-assisted enzyme design — already published practice

every layer exists. the adventure is the joining.

how it would work

two technologies, and which one is allowed to decide

the second act

two ends of one spectrum

logic — crystal

truth survives composition. a chain of a million inferences loses nothing.

the price: the world must be curated into symbols first, and one wrong symbol poisons everything downstream — silently, permanently.

ML — weather

touches the raw world without asking permission — noisy spectra, missing labels, patterns nobody formalised.

the price: nothing composes. chain two outputs and errors do not add, they breed. and it cannot decline.

logic fails at the entrance — getting the world in. ML fails at the exit — getting trust out.

the same object, twice

pixels — logic

a decision you can point at, and defend.

gradient — ML

a value everywhere, and nowhere to draw the line.

equivalence is not similarity

equivalencesimilarity
transitiveyes — A=B, B=C gives A=Cno — it leaks across chains
shapeclean disjoint classesoverlapping neighbourhoods
valuebinary — same or notgraded — a number
licensessubstitutiononly an ordering
carries a witnessyes — and whyno
similarity ranks. equivalence licenses replacement.

and every real equivalence is manufactured — by declaring which differences do not count. same molecule, up to protonation. the ChEBI join failed because two such declarations collided, and neither was written down.

the space

10¹¹

points in the design space

10⁶

points the robot will ever visit

variants × substrates × conditions — against a working lifetime of screening

you will see one ten-thousandth of one percent.

so choosing where to look is not a preliminary to the science. it is the science.

finding is hard, checking is cheap

the space of candidate answers is enormous. validating one candidate is bounded work.

ML has the ideas. logic has the veto.

the inexact, cheap, creative technology goes on the expensive side; the exact one goes where exactness is affordable — and whatever sits in the veto seat must be auditable, re-runnable by someone who does not trust it.

search has two halves

1 · feasible?2 · how promising?
answerbinarycontinuous
checkableyes, before running anythingnot until tested
costa lookupa model
carries a witnessyes — not in inventory, no supplier under six weeksno — 0.83 has no reason attached

feasibility runs first, and as a generator — it defines the space that is sampled, rather than sieving a list already produced.

the trap

tierexamplegenuinely binary?
knownin stock · codon valid · already tested · assay covers ityes — certifiable
predictedwill it fold? will it express? soluble at 40 °C?no — a prediction in binary clothes
rankedactivity · selectivityno, and openly so

exclude what the model doubts, never test it, never contradict it — the blind spot never heals.

wrongly excluded is silent and permanent; wrongly included costs one well and corrects itself. so be strict where the constraint is a fact, generous where it is a prediction — demote, never delete.

two ways to search

both are sound — everything either one returns is genuinely feasible. only the left is complete.

so the right can prove something exists. it can never prove that nothing does.

the border crossing

possible, then promising, then true — and only the last of the three returns a pixel rather than a gradient.

nothing enters the ledger without a stamp.

and it may refuse

  • the query is shown in prose before it runs — the only check on intent that exists
  • the answer arrives with its derivation, re-runnable by someone who does not trust the system
  • an empty answer is diagnosed, never returned bare — which clause killed it, and what would return something
  • similarity is available but never silently promoted to identity
  • and the system may say: I could not turn your question into a query I can justify
a system that fails well is worth more than one that always answers.

from molecule to process —

with nothing lost on the way.
